[INBO 2025 — question paper]
34. (2 points) A geneticist was studying the cell cycle in the root tip cells of a plant. She
microscopically observed that 15 cells were in prophase, 7 cells were in prometaphase, 8
cells were in metaphase, 7 were in anaphase, 5 were in telophase and 88 were in interphase.
The overall cell cycle for this particular species was recorded to be 23 hours. The time span
that the cells are in the mitotic phase is:
Note that the final answer for the question will be given marks only if calculations are shown
in the box given and the final answer is filled in the blank.

[CBSE Class XII Biology, marking scheme, 2025-26]

items.stem: In a cell culture, 20% of the cells are in mitosis. If the total cell cycle time is 18 hours, how long does the mitotic phase last?
Which of the following is true about the cell cycle as described in the passage?
A cell has 16 chromosomes at the end of G1 phase. How many chromosomes will it have after S phase and after M phase, respectively?
What happens to the chromosomes during anaphase?
If a cell has 46 chromosomes in its nucleus, how many chromosomes will each daughter cell have after mitosis?
A scientist counted 100 cells in a tissue sample. Out of these, 20 were in anaphase. If the total cell cycle time is 12 hours, how long does anaphase last?
Which of the following is a key feature of metaphase?
Which phase of the cell cycle is marked by the alignment of chromosomes at the equatorial plate?
If the cell cycle of a mammalian cell is 24 hours and 80% of the time is spent in interphase, how many hours are spent in the mitotic phase?
Based on the diagram, which of the following best represents the metaphase plate?
Based on the diagram of the cell cycle, which stage is characterised by the separation of sister chromatids?
Why is cytokinesis different in plant and animal cells?
If a cell spends 10 hours in interphase and 2 hours in mitosis, what is the percentage of time spent in mitosis?
Which of the following is a characteristic of telophase?

A student counted 25 cells in prophase, 10 in metaphase, 5 in anaphase, and 10 in telophase, while 130 cells were in interphase. If the total cell cycle duration is 18 hours, how many hours does the mitotic phase last?
Based on the passage, what is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
Which phase of meiosis I is marked by the formation of the synaptonemal complex?
Which of the following is the correct order of stages in mitosis?
During which phase of meiosis is the nuclear envelope reformed?
If a cell spends 80% of its cycle in interphase and the total cycle is 20 hours, how many hours does it spend in mitosis?
What is the main purpose of crossing over during meiosis?
If a cell has 20 chromosomes in its diploid state, how many chromosomes will it have after meiosis II?
Which stage of mitosis is characterised by the alignment of chromosomes at the equator?
Why is meiosis essential for sexual reproduction?

A researcher observed 100 cells in a sample and found that 20 cells were in prophase, 10 in metaphase, 15 in anaphase, 10 in telophase, and 45 in interphase. If the total cell cycle duration is 12 hours, how many hours do the cells spend in the mitotic phase?
Based on the diagram of the cell cycle in Figure 10.1, which phase is responsible for the division of the cytoplasm?

A geneticist observed 15 cells in prophase, 7 in prometaphase, 8 in metaphase, 7 in anaphase, 5 in telophase, and 88 in interphase. The overall cell cycle duration is 23 hours. What is the time spent in the mitotic phase?
Which phase of the cell cycle is described as the resting phase, but is actually the time when the cell is preparing for division?
What is the term used for the sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells?
If a cell has 2C DNA content during the G1 phase, what will be its DNA content after the S phase?
What is the term used for the sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome and divides into two daughter cells?
Which phase of the cell cycle is the longest?
Which phase of the cell cycle is marked by DNA replication and chromosome duplication?
If a cell is in the G phase of the cell cycle, what is it likely doing?
If a cell is observed to have its chromosomes aligned at the metaphase plate, which of the following is most likely to occur next?
If a cell has 2C DNA content at G1 phase, what will be the DNA content after S phase and after M phase, respectively?
